paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and high temperature strength at 1773 K of Nbss/Nb5Si3 composites alloyed with molybdenum

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Nbss/Nb5Si3 composites alloyed with and without Mo, where Nbss denotes Nb solid solution, are prepared by various processes such as arc-melting (AM), isothermal forging (IF), directional solidification (DS) and powder metallurgy (PM), followed by heat treatment at 1973 and 2123 K.

evidence.section: Conclusions
evidence.quote: Dispersed microstructure leads to an increase in yield strength at 1773 K more effectively than an aggregate structure in binary Nb ss/Nb5Si3 alloys.

evidence.section: 3.1. Microstructure of binary and Mo-added ternary Nbss/Nb5Si3 composites
evidence.quote: The nominal compositions are Nb-10 at.%Si (a, b, hereafter denoted as Nb-10Si), Nb-18Si (c,d) and Nb-22Si (e). X-ray diffraction and EPMA results indicated that all the binary alloys were composed of Nbss and Nb5Si3 phases without any other phases or inclusions.

evidence.section: 2. Experimental procedure
evidence.quote: Small alloy buttons were produced by arc-melting under an argon atmosphere on a water-cooled copper hearth, using a non-consumable tungsten electrode. The alloy buttons were re-melted at least 3 times to assure the chemical homogeneity of constituent elements, and then they were re-melted together on a rectangular shaped copper hearth to make a specimen with large dimensions.

evidence.section: 3.1. Microstructure of binary and Mo-added ternary Nbss/Nb5Si3 composites
evidence.quote: With increasing Si content the microstructures of AM alloys changed from a hypo-eutectic consisting of dendritic primary Nbss and eutectic (Nbss+Nb5Si3) to a hyper-eutectic consisting of primary Nb5Si3 and eutectic (Nbss+Nb5Si3).
